t: You're looking at a bronze statue of George IV on horseback, in Trafalgar Square. He's dressed in ancient Roman clothes and rides without a saddle. The sculptor was Sir Francis Chantrey, the leading portrait sculptor of Regency Britain, who also made the statue of George III at the Guildhall. The statue was originally designed to sit on top of the Marble Arch at the entrance to Buckingham Palace, but it was placed here after the king's death in 1830. George IV had been prince regent from 1811 before becoming king in 1820.
